Keysight reported a record quarter in which earnings per share came in well above what had been expected and net income roughly doubled from a year earlier [C25]. Communications Solutions Group revenue grew by more than two fifths while its operating income grew faster still [C28]. Management now expects fourth quarter revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 [C1].

Supply will govern near-term revenue for several quarters, so booked demand may not reach the income statement when the market expects [C33]. The fourth-quarter revenue range sits only slightly above the quarter just reported, and analysts questioned that modest sequential guide [C31] [C32]. A one-time tariff boost lifted profitability and will not repeat, which raises the bar margins have to clear [C34] [C15]. The market is arguing about whether the valuation leaves room for error [C19].

The plan buys in three tranches at the support bands beneath the price, each an equal share of a full position [C10]. It sells an equal share at each traded resistance band above but the top one, and from the top one holds the last share on a stop trailed under the price rather than selling it at a price [C11]. In an uptrend each tranche's stop is raised to the higher of the band beneath it and the last swing low beneath it [C12].
